cards.title: Fixes from Critical Finding #1 (ADR-0017) and Principal Engineer audit 2.1/2.2/2.3
items: AG feedback surfaces at its own interrupt() (ag_feedback_review), never passed straight to Findings Author — only Lead/Approver confirmation routes back to draft_findings for a real redraft, drawn as an actual loop-back edge, not left to prose

New checkpoint: Pre-AG Sign-off (ADR-0003's third named checkpoint, "before anything is submitted for Assistant Governor approval") — distinct from Findings Sign-off, which approves findings[] data before the letter is even drafted; this one reviews the drafted transmittal letter/pre-exit deck itself, right before ag_status moves to awaiting_ag

Both redraft loops (AG feedback, pre-exit concerns) route back through the same draft_findings → findings_signoff → pre_ag_signoff path — a redraft re-evaluates severity against the current rubric version (ADR-0020) and must pass both sign-offs again before reaching the AG a second time
Persisted severity must equal rubric.lookup()'s return value, enforced in code

cards.title: How to read this diagram
items: Branch points (e.g. AG showcase's approved/changes-requested split) are edge-labeled, not drawn as decision diamonds — archify's workflow grammar has no decision-node/fork-join primitive, so guard conditions live on the edge label, not a gateway shape
Closest standard: a UML activity diagram without gateway notation. Human checkpoints use a dedicated lane, not a person-icon convention

Pre-Exit Meeting's "no concerns" path (not drawn as a separate edge) is the terminal state — preexit_status: proceeded_to_exit — matching the Examiner Dashboard's auto-close condition (lfi-examiner-dashboard-userflow-v1.html)
